assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Catalyst
items.clue: Something that speeds up a chemical reaction and is not used up.

items.label: Chemical bond
items.clue: The force that holds two atoms together in a molecule or compound

items.label: Neutralisation
items.clue: A reaction that moves the pH towards 7 and makes a salt and water.

items.label: Base
items.clue: A substance that can neutralise an acid; a soluble one is called an alkali

questions.stem: Zinc reacts with hydrochloric acid. One product is zinc chloride. What is the other product?

options.text: Water, which stays in the beaker
Hydrogen gas, which fizzes off
Oxygen gas, which fizzes off
Zinc oxide, a white solid

questions.explanation: Yes. metal + acid → salt + hydrogen. The salt here is zinc chloride, and the bubbles of gas are hydrogen.

questions.stem: Magnesium reacts with sulfuric acid. Which salt is made?

options.text: Sodium chloride
Magnesium acid
Magnesium chloride
Magnesium sulfate

questions.explanation: Yes. Sulfuric acid makes sulfates, and the first part of the name comes from the metal: magnesium sulfate.

questions.stem: Magnesium is added to hydrochloric acid and it fizzes. Which test shows that the gas is hydrogen?

options.text: A lit splint gives a squeaky pop
A glowing splint bursts into flame
It turns clear limewater milky
It turns damp blue litmus red

questions.explanation: Yes. Hydrogen burns with a squeaky pop when a lit splint is held at the mouth of the tube.

questions.stem: Magnesium ribbon is added to hydrochloric acid. It fizzes and slowly disappears. Where has the magnesium gone?

options.text: It has been eaten away to nothing by the acid
It has changed into the bubbles of hydrogen
It is now in magnesium chloride, in solution
It is still magnesium, just mixed into the acid

questions.explanation: Yes. The magnesium atoms are in the salt, magnesium chloride, which stays dissolved in the solution. Evaporating the water would leave it.

questions.stem: Which general word equation shows an acid reacting with a metal?

options.text: acid + metal → salt + water
acid + metal → salt + hydrogen
acid + metal → salt + oxygen
acid + metal → salt + carbon dioxide

questions.explanation: A metal reacts with an acid to make a salt and hydrogen gas.

questions.stem: A piece of copper is put into dilute hydrochloric acid. No bubbles are seen. Why?

options.text: The acid is too weak to react with any metal
The hydrogen made has dissolved in the acid
Copper reacts with alkalis but not with acids
Copper is too unreactive to react with this acid

questions.explanation: Copper is a very unreactive metal, so it does not react with dilute acids and no hydrogen is made.

questions.stem: Zinc reacts with hydrochloric acid and hydrogen gas is given off. Where do the hydrogen atoms come from?

options.text: They were inside the zinc metal
They came from the air above the acid
They were part of the acid
They were newly made in the reaction

questions.explanation: Acids contain hydrogen; the metal takes its place to form a salt, and the hydrogen is released as gas.

questions.stem: In chemistry, what is a salt?

options.text: Sodium chloride and nothing else: the salt put on food
A compound made when a metal replaces an acid's hydrogen
Any white, crystalline solid that dissolves in water
A mixture of an acid with a metal stirred into it

questions.explanation: A salt is a compound formed when the hydrogen in an acid is replaced by a metal.

questions.stem: Magnesium is added to an acid. The fizzing stops, but some magnesium is left. Why has it stopped?

options.text: All of the acid has now reacted
The magnesium has run out of hydrogen
The liquid is now full of hydrogen gas
The leftover magnesium is really a salt

questions.explanation: The reaction stops when one reactant runs out; magnesium is left over, so the acid is used up.
